admission.justification: The five parametrised file/base/route shapes pin the population the item check reads: an open file is judged, the leaf's own closed file is judged at its publication, and a closed file at a master route or closed by an earlier frozen closeout is not. Restoring the base-filtered population fails two of the five, so the regression cannot pass unnoticed.

applicability: Every R09-history-rows item-token judgment over converted memory: at a leaf's publication (closeout, direct landing, recorded landing), at a master's checkpoint, at a master-level landing and at a sync.
conditions: An open history file is item-judged at every route.
At a leaf publication the leaf's own history file is item-judged whatever its `closed` flag says, when neither a comparison base nor a frozen commit holds it closed.

At a master's checkpoint, a master-level landing or a sync, a closed history file of one of the master's leaves is covered by MIK-R52 rule 5 (closed, owned by a leaf the master accounts for, byte-identical to that owner's recorded publication) instead of being item-judged here.
exclusions: A history file closed in a comparison base, or closed by an earlier non-integrated closeout of the same leaf: historical, and outside both history checks.
The unknown-subject rule, which still reads every history file at every route; the merge rule `R09-history-rows-merged`, the hidden-change rule and MIK-R22 rule 7.
statement: A leaf publication validates every item of its own newly published history, while history item checks and re-anchor checks use the same checked_history_files scope.
